intro: The forty-seventh screen read 90 pictures, the set's 21 and 69 probes, with twelve readers and four scorers: 946 of 992 scored items had full marks, and one was misread. **Grown figures are read as grown, and two templates fall under the legibility gate.** The four grown figures that v0.49's readers called a girl or a boy first in 20 of their 89 pictures are called so in 3 of 79. What did it was measured before it was built: pictures of v0.49's own screen were built again with four casts and read blind, and marks of age with a smaller head left one young name in 45 appearances, where v0.49's cast had 13. The seesaw's children sit on the plank, set down by their own measured underside, and no reader of ten pictures has one above it. The lost balloon, its string's end by the child in the garden too, reads 1.00 in five pictures. The gate passes 62 of the 64 templates. `play_catch` fails at 0.80 in five pictures: a ball drawn by a grown catcher's hands was read as hers to throw. `square_wheel` fails at 0.875 in four, on its one wheelbarrow, whose square wheel a reader took for a hose reel, the sprinkler's hose lying behind it. Neither drawing was changed in this release, and nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one. The set's score fell to 0.949 from 0.967; nine of its eighteen items under full marks are the clouds or a tree, left out by a reader. And many full marks still carry a hedge: on the strict count 52 of the 64 templates pass, for v0.49's 54.
design:
## Design tests

The cast of builder 0.50.0 and revision 47's rules were read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v050.md`, eight pictures, one fresh reader each). The bench had read each change on its own; here a reader has them at a picture's size. Between them the eight forced sets hold nine of the ten people, the seesaw twice, the lost balloon, the stopped hose, the goat on its stake, a held balloon, the fence painter and the slide. Seven placed on their first seed and one on its second. One forced set was changed before any picture of it existed, a shopper who cannot be forced in the playground giving way to a pram. One picture was built twice before any reader had it: on my look at the eight its empty seesaw had the old T handles where a ridden seesaw now has grab bars, and the empty one was given the same bars. No picture was built again after a reading.

Every forced event was read, twenty-four of twenty-four. That is a count of what a reader wrote about a picture built to show the event; it is not the screen, where a scorer who has not seen the picture marks each item against the description. What the readers wrote:
- **The seesaw,** twice: "She is sitting on the raised left end of the seesaw, holding the handle." Neither reader has a rider above the plank: "Nothing appears to be floating or passing through anything else." The grown rider's seat is v0.31's note still: "he might be sitting on the low end of the plank, or on the ground right next to it".
- **The lost balloon:** "The red balloon looks like it has escaped, and its string is trailing down out of his reach." The second reading is still offered: "Or it could be loose and unrelated to him."
- **The stopped hose,** v0.49's drawing: "If the dog is on the hose, it may be stepping on it and blocking the water, which could explain why the boy seems to be looking at the nozzle."
- **The goat's stake:** "The goat is tied by a rope to a short wooden stake in the ground."
- **A held balloon's string:** "is walking or running to the left while holding the string of a red balloon".
- **The painter's pole:** "She holds a long-handled blue paint roller up against the fence."

**Who the figures were called.** The four grown figures that v0.49's screen had called young appear ten times in the eight pictures and are called by a young name first once, where v0.49's design tests had four of nine. The one is the man in the red shirt with an ice cream at his mouth, where the cone hides his moustache: "boy or young man with brown hair, in a red T-shirt and blue trousers". The woman in purple is a "woman with dark hair, purple top, teal trousers, black shoes", and the man in green a "man with a beard and short dark hair, green t-shirt, beige trousers, brown shoes". Nothing was mended after the readings; each remark went to the screen's list.
redrawn: `seesaw` and `seesaw_heavy`, their children seated by measure, read 1.00 in five pictures each, as they did in three; what changed is the remark, and no reader has a rider above the plank. `lost_balloon` reads 1.00 in five pictures, from 0.972 in six. `goat_grazing`, `balloon` and `paint_fence` read 1.00 as before, in five, five and nine pictures. `blocked_hose`, benched without its swelling and left, reads 0.95 on two half marks in one picture, where v0.49's 1.00 carried six calls; `slide` reads 1.00 in five. Of the templates looked at and left, `play_catch` went from 1.00 in four pictures to 0.80 in five and fails, and the three dog templates hold 1.00 by the gate and carry hedges on the strict count. `square_wheel`, `bird_steals` and `ducks_bread`, each 1.00 in v0.49 and none of them on this release's list, read 0.875, 0.90 and 0.944. It is one screen, of 9 to 20 items a template, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.025 to 0.056: v0.49's 1.00 for `play_catch` was one reader's doubt from this, and its strict count said so (0.812).
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (32 in three, 10 in four, 17 in five, 2 in six, 1 in nine, 1 in thirteen and 1 in sixteen). 62 of the 64 pass, where all 64 did in v0.49 and 63 in v0.48 and in v0.47. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. Two fail: `play_catch` (0.80 on ten items in five pictures) and `square_wheel` (0.875 on twelve items in four pictures, with a misread). Three more are under 1.00 and pass: `bird_steals` (0.90), `ducks_bread` (0.944) and `blocked_hose` (0.95); the other 59 read 1.00. Per angle (`vision/v050/gate_yaw.json`), 18 of the 19 (template, angle) pairs pass; the thief bird at three-quarters has 0.833 on nine items in three pictures. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 33 full marks that stand beside another reading halved, 52 of the 64 pass. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
calib: 44 of the calibration's 252 numbers moved by 0.002 or more, where 24 had in v0.49: every grown figure is drawn anew, and revision 47's rules move three templates. The largest move is `lost_balloon`'s inference (s from -1.163 to -1.071), its string's end now by the child in the garden too; no other s moved by more than 0.04. The planner's priors moved with them, and with the new prior it drew other sets: five of the sixteen cells have v0.49's templates, where thirteen of v0.49's had v0.48's. The calibration was measured once, with the cast and the rules as they are released.
inspection: Every cell of the set was built under revision 47, with the new cast and its prior. Tiers 1 to 3 placed on their showcase seeds; five of the sixteen cells have v0.49's templates and eleven are new sets. The tier-4 park, street and playground placed on v0.49's seeds with v0.49's templates. The tier-4 garden failed on v0.49's base and on three more, forty steps each, and placed on v0.48's base at its seventh step; v0.49's set for that cell, forced, placed on none of eight seeds, with the lost balloon's new rule on or off. The isomorphs are five: two of tier 2, two of tier 3 and one of tier 4, the last on v0.49's seed, third call. The probe pass built 58 and left one template short, the begging dog; three small forced groups filled it, and the pass stratified by angle added 8: 69 probes, 37 gardens, 18 parks, 12 playgrounds and 2 streets. **I looked at every picture on sheets before any reader had it, found nothing to mend, and built none again after that look.** All 90 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 385 of 385. Its soft palette warning is raised by 329 records (332 of 389 in v0.49), with the median share of a figure's pixels on a palette colour as it was, 0.88. The target was not loosened.
